sections.h2: What is Hamilton County, Florida like for a property owner?
sections.html:
Hamilton County is a rural county in north central Florida with Georgia along its northern edge. Its county website calls it a peninsula within a peninsula, bounded by the Withlacoochee River on the west and the Suwannee River on the east and south, with the Alapaha River, known as the "River of Sand", running through the middle.

The county seat is Jasper, and the tax collector's millage table also lists the municipalities of Jennings and White Springs. The county's page puts the estimated population at 14,799 and notes that Hamilton County sits at the crossroads of I-75 and I-10, within reach of Jacksonville, Gainesville and Tallahassee. For a seller, that mix of farmland, small towns and highway access shapes who buys, and the tax bill depends on whether the parcel sits inside a town.

The county also reports a moratorium on single-site RV and camper living, with no electric permits issued for RVs. If the property you plan to sell has an RV hookup, ask the county before listing.

sections.h2: Which Hamilton County offices handle the tax bill?
sections.html:
The property appraiser, the tax collector and the clerk each own one step. The appraiser sets value and exemptions, the collector bills and collects, and the clerk runs the value adjustment board and tax deed sales.

  • Property appraiser: values every parcel, keeps the exemption rolls, and handles name, address and legal description changes. Call or visit the office in Jasper before March 1 to file for homestead.
  • Tax collector: online at hamiltontaxcollector.com, with a parcel search and online payment.
  • Clerk and value adjustment board: 207 NE 1st Street, Room 106, Jasper, phone 386-792-1288.
  • County commission: sets the county millage rate and handles questions such as the RV rule above.

Confirm office hours by phone before you drive in, since county offices post their own schedules.

sections.h2: What does the Hamilton County millage table show?
sections.html:
The tax collector publishes a table headed "Hamilton 2026 millage", in decimal form. Treat it as the collector's published listing and compare it with your TRIM notice and November bill.

Only one town line applies to a given parcel. A rural parcel carries the county, school and water lines, while a house in Jasper adds the Jasper line. Non-ad valorem assessments are separate, flat charges for services such as fire or solid waste, and they show up on the same bill.

sections.h2: When are Hamilton County property taxes due and when are they late?
sections.html:
Statements go out on or before November 1 each year, and the tax collector lists discounts of 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. The tax lien attaches January 1 of the tax year, the full amount is payable before April 1, and the bill is delinquent from April 1.

At delinquency, a 3 percent penalty is added to real estate tax and the unpaid parcel is advertised in the local paper starting in May. Unpaid tangible personal property adds 1.5 percent per month. The collector holds an online tax certificate sale at the end of May or on June 1.

The state calendar adds the front end: the appraiser values property as of January 1, exemption applications are due March 1, TRIM notices go out in August, and a value challenge petition is due within 25 days of the TRIM notice, per the Department of Revenue.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Hamilton County assessment?
sections.html:
You petition the value adjustment board through the clerk. The board only decides whether property is appraised at fair market value and whether an agricultural classification or exemption should be approved. It cannot change a value because you cannot afford the tax, and it has no control over rates.

  • The filing fee is $15, and $5 more for each extra parcel when contiguous parcels are combined on one petition.
  • If the property appraiser or tax collector denied a timely homestead exemption or homestead tax deferral, there is no fee.
  • Petitions need an original signature, and copies or faxes are not accepted.
  • A late petition is sent to the board attorney, and a hearing is set only for good cause.

The clerk encourages you to speak with the property appraiser before filing. The state form is DR-486, and a postmark by the deadline does not save a petition that arrives after it.

sections.h2: How do homestead, caps and deferral work in Hamilton County?
sections.html:
The statewide homestead exemption is up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 applying to school taxes too, per the state homestead guide. File by March 1, and note that the property must be your permanent residence on January 1.

After the first year, the Save Our Homes cap holds assessed value growth to the lower of 3 percent or CPI. A sale or other change of ownership resets value to just value the following January 1, so a buyer will not inherit your capped value. If you plan to buy again in Florida, portability can carry part of the cap to a new homestead within three years.

The deferral program on Form DR-570 is due to the tax collector by March 31 and covers tax above a share of household income. Hamilton County owners who think they qualify should ask the collector for the form before that date.

sections.h2: What if a Hamilton County property goes to a tax deed sale?
sections.html:
The clerk conducts the sale after a certificate holder applies. Hamilton County's tax deed page warns that every property is sold buyer beware and as is, with no promises about title, zoning or condition. It also points to s. 197.542(2), which requires the high bidder to post a nonrefundable deposit.

State law lets a holder apply two years after April 1 of the year the certificate was issued. The opening bid on homestead land includes half of the latest assessed value on top of the amounts due. An owner can still stop the process by paying the tax collector what is owed before the sale. If a sale is already advertised on your house, treat that date as the working deadline for any plan to sell.

sections.h2: What should I know when selling a Hamilton County house with tax due?
sections.html:
Tell the closing agent about every unpaid year at the start. The agent orders a payoff from the tax collector and pays it at closing from your proceeds, so a sale can clear the lien without cash up front from you.

The deed is subject to Florida documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and the Revenue Department says every party to the document is liable. The clerk collects it at recording. Ask for the settlement statement ahead of the closing date so the tax lines and the recording charges are no surprise. A buyer who pays cash can usually close on a short timeline, which matters when April 1 or a sale date is near.

faqs.q: When is Hamilton County property tax delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. The tax collector says statements go out on or before November 1, and a 3 percent penalty is added to unpaid real estate tax on April 1.

faqs.q: What is the early payment discount in Hamilton County?
faqs.a: It is 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February, per the Hamilton County Tax Collector.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to appeal a Hamilton County value?
faqs.a: The value adjustment board filing fee is $15, plus $5 for each additional contiguous parcel. A petition over a denied homestead exemption or homestead deferral carries no fee.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hamilton County property that has a tax certificate on it?
faqs.a: Yes. The certificate is a lien, and the payoff to the tax collector is made at closing so the buyer receives clean title. Request a payoff that includes interest and charges.

faqs.q: Does the property appraiser set my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The county commission, school board, towns and districts set the rates. The appraiser sets value and handles exemptions.
